statement: For every natural number n (including zero), every direction d∈{lower,upper}, every ops:Arithmetic, every real matrix T:I_n×I_n→R, every vector b:I_n→R and every u∈R, assume 0≤u, Triangular(d,T), det(T)≠0, n u<1, and ExecutionValid(u,d,ops,T,b). Here I_n={0,...,n-1} is Fin n and n u uses the real cast of n. Set x̂=computedSolution(d,ops,T,b), the actual sweep from the zero vector with the supplied four operation fields and specified traversal and dot-product orders. There exists a real matrix ΔT:I_n×I_n→R such that (T+ΔT)x̂=b, Triangular(d,ΔT), and ∀i,j∈I_n, |ΔT_ij|≤gamma(n,u)|T_ij|=[n u/(1-n u)]|T_ij|. The vector equality means ∀i∈I_n, sum over all j∈I_n of (T_ij+ΔT_ij)x̂_j equals b_i. The existential perturbation may depend on all quantified inputs and their execution. Thus the constructed vector is an exact solution for a componentwise bounded perturbation with the same triangular zero pattern; the conclusion does not assert exact solution of the unperturbed system. The construction descriptions use R for the real numbers, I_n for Fin n, T_i for the function j↦T_ij, and j::J for a list with head j and tail J. All operations outside the supplied ops fields are ordinary real operations.

targets.name: Research.TriangularSolve.solution_of_a_triangular_system
targets.statement: For every natural number n (including zero), every direction d∈{lower,upper}, every ops:Arithmetic, every real matrix T:I_n×I_n→R, every vector b:I_n→R and every u∈R, assume 0≤u, Triangular(d,T), det(T)≠0, n u<1, and ExecutionValid(u,d,ops,T,b). constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.Direction
constructions.description: An inductive type with exactly two nullary constructors lower and upper, and no fields. It selects the zero pattern and orders below.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.Arithmetic
constructions.description: A structure with one constructor Arithmetic.mk taking four arbitrary functions R×R→R, in order mul, add, sub, div. These are its four fields. The structure contains no accuracy laws, algebraic laws, format, or rounding procedure; it is supplied function data.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.RelativeRound
constructions.description: For real u,e,c, RelativeRound(u,e,c) means there exists δ∈R with |δ|≤u and c=e(1+δ). Each occurrence has its own existential witness. In particular an exact argument zero forces a computed value zero whenever the relation holds.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.gamma
constructions.description: For every n∈N and u∈R, gamma(n,u)=n u/(1-n u), with n cast to R. The definition has no restrictions on n or u and uses the formal real division operation, which is total (division by zero is zero). The theorem supplies n u<1.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.Triangular
constructions.description: For any n∈N, direction d and T:I_n×I_n→R, Triangular(lower,T) means ∀i,j∈I_n, i<j implies T_ij=0. Triangular(upper,T) means ∀i,j∈I_n, j<i implies T_ij=0. No condition on diagonal entries is included.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.rowOrder
constructions.description: For d:Direction and n∈N, rowOrder(lower,n)=[0,1,...,n-1] as a list in I_n, and rowOrder(upper,n) is its reverse [n-1,...,0]. For n=0 both lists are empty.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.previousColumns
constructions.description: For n∈N, d:Direction and i∈I_n, filter rowOrder(d,n), retaining j<i for lower and i<j for upper. Thus previousColumns(lower,i)=[0,...,i-1] and previousColumns(upper,i)=[n-1,...,i+1], in those orders.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.dotAcc
constructions.description: For n∈N, ops:Arithmetic, a,x:I_n→R, list L over I_n and c∈R, define A([],c)=c and A(j::J,c)=A(J,ops.add(c,ops.mul(a_j,x_j))). dotAcc(ops,a,x,L,c)=A(L,c). It accumulates computed products from left to right. Arbitrary finite lists, including repetitions, are accepted.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.roundedDot
constructions.description: For n∈N, ops:Arithmetic, a,x:I_n→R and list L over I_n, roundedDot(ops,a,x,[])=0; roundedDot(ops,a,x,j::J)=dotAcc(ops,a,x,J,ops.mul(a_j,x_j)). A nonempty dot product starts with the first computed product and adds the remaining computed products in list order, without an initial addition to zero. Its name does not impose a rounding law.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.DotAccValid
constructions.description: A recursively defined proposition, not a numerical algorithm. For n∈N, u∈R, ops:Arithmetic, a,x:I_n→R, list L over I_n and c∈R, write V(L,c)=DotAccValid(u,ops,a,x,L,c). V([],c)=true. For j::J let q=ops.mul(a_j,x_j) and r=ops.add(c,q). Then V(j::J,c) is the conjunction RelativeRound(u,a_j x_j,q), RelativeRound(u,c+q,r), and V(J,r). The exact products and sums here use ordinary real operations. This checks the operations along the actual accumulator trajectory.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.DotValid
constructions.description: For n∈N, u∈R, ops:Arithmetic, a,x:I_n→R and list L over I_n, DotValid(u,ops,a,x,[])=true. For L=j::J it is RelativeRound(u,a_j x_j,q) ∧ DotAccValid(u,ops,a,x,J,q), where q=ops.mul(a_j,x_j). This proposition checks exactly the multiplications and additions used by roundedDot, including the absence of an initial addition to zero.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.rowNumerator
constructions.description: For n∈N, d:Direction, ops:Arithmetic, T:I_n×I_n→R, b,x:I_n→R and i∈I_n, let L=previousColumns(d,i) and T_i(j)=T_ij. If L is empty, rowNumerator(d,ops,T,b,x,i)=b_i. Otherwise it is ops.sub(b_i,roundedDot(ops,T_i,x,L)). No subtraction is performed for an empty L.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.solveRow
constructions.description: For n∈N, d:Direction, ops:Arithmetic, T:I_n×I_n→R, b,x:I_n→R and i∈I_n, solveRow(d,ops,T,b,x,i) returns y:I_n→R with y_i=ops.div(rowNumerator(d,ops,T,b,x,i),T_ii) and y_k=x_k for every k∈I_n with k≠i. It updates a single coordinate. Its definition imposes no triangularity or nonzero-diagonal hypothesis.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.RowValid
constructions.description: For n∈N, u∈R, d:Direction, ops:Arithmetic, T:I_n×I_n→R, b,x:I_n→R and i∈I_n, put L=previousColumns(d,i), s=roundedDot(ops,T_i,x,L), and r=rowNumerator(d,ops,T,b,x,i). RowValid(u,d,ops,T,b,x,i) is the conjunction of DotValid(u,ops,T_i,x,L); the condition RelativeRound(u,b_i-s,ops.sub(b_i,s)) if L is nonempty (true if L is empty); and RelativeRound(u,r/T_ii,ops.div(r,T_ii)). The exact subtraction and division are ordinary real operations. It is a proposition on the operations at the current vector x, not a global accuracy law for the fields.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.solveRows
constructions.description: For n∈N, d:Direction, ops:Arithmetic, T:I_n×I_n→R, b:I_n→R, list L over I_n and starting vector x:I_n→R, let S([],x)=x and S(i::J,x)=S(J,solveRow(d,ops,T,b,x,i)). solveRows(d,ops,T,b,L,x)=S(L,x). It processes rows in the supplied list order, passing each updated vector onward. The list may repeat or omit rows.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.RowsValid
constructions.description: A recursively defined proposition. For n∈N, u∈R, d:Direction, ops:Arithmetic, T:I_n×I_n→R, b:I_n→R, list L over I_n and x:I_n→R, let W([],x)=true and W(i::J,x)=RowValid(u,d,ops,T,b,x,i) ∧ W(J,solveRow(d,ops,T,b,x,i)). RowsValid(u,d,ops,T,b,L,x)=W(L,x). These conditions follow the same intermediate vectors as solveRows; this is not a separate numerical algorithm.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.computedSolution
constructions.description: For n∈N, d:Direction, ops:Arithmetic, T:I_n×I_n→R and b:I_n→R, computedSolution(d,ops,T,b)=solveRows(d,ops,T,b,rowOrder(d,n),0), where 0 is the identically zero vector. It performs one increasing sweep for lower or decreasing sweep for upper, using the specified ordered dot products and single-coordinate updates. It does not itself enforce rounding accuracy or solve by forming an inverse.

constructions.name: Research.TriangularSolve.ExecutionValid
constructions.description: For n∈N, u∈R, d:Direction, ops:Arithmetic, T:I_n×I_n→R and b:I_n→R, ExecutionValid(u,d,ops,T,b)=RowsValid(u,d,ops,T,b,rowOrder(d,n),0), with the identically zero initial vector. This proposition requires the local relative-error conditions on the actual sweep defining computedSolution. It is not an additional numerical algorithm or a requirement of accuracy on all possible field inputs.

assumptions: All vectors and matrices are functions on the finite index sets stated above; all scalars are real. Every n in a construction is an implicit natural-number parameter except the explicit n of rowOrder and gamma. Lists are finite ordered lists, with no distinctness assumption unless generated by rowOrder or previousColumns.
The target universally quantifies the implicit parameter n∈N and explicit parameters d:Direction, ops:Arithmetic, T:I_n×I_n→R, b:I_n→R, u∈R.
Target hypothesis: Triangular(d,T), namely ∀i,j∈I_n, T_ij=0 if i<j for lower, or if j<i for upper.
Target hypothesis: n u<1. Together with 0≤u this makes 1-n u positive and gamma(n,u) nonnegative.

Target hypothesis: ExecutionValid(u,d,ops,T,b), expanded by the recursive validity predicates in the constructions. Every local witness δ is real with |δ|≤u and computed=exact(1+δ). Only the operations used by this execution are constrained.

Arithmetic has no built-in accuracy or algebraic assumptions. The construction definitions have no nonsingularity, triangularity, or sign requirements beyond what their explicit validity predicates state. There is no supplied hypothesis on a machine format, representability, or global rounding behavior.
